Introduction Fire accidents and gas leakages are common hazards in homes, shops, and small businesses. These incidents can cause serious damage to property and may also threaten human life.​ ​ Most workplaces rely on basic safety systems such as fire extinguishers and smoke alarms, which require human presence. However, fires or gas leaks may occur when no one is present, leading to delayed response.​ ​ This project proposes a Firefighting and Gas Detection Robot that can automatically detect fire and gas leakage, provide alerts, and assist in extinguishing small fires. 2. Proposed Methodology The development of the Firefighting and Gas Detection Robot will be carried out through several structured steps, combining hardware implementation and software control. 2.1 Hardware Setup At the initial stage, all physical components of the robot will be assembled. ●​ A PVC board or robot chassis will be used as the base platform. ●​ Two DC motors with wheels will be mounted to enable movement. ●​ The ESP32 microcontroller will be installed as the main control unit. ●​ The motor driver (L298N) will be connected to control the motors. ●​ A battery pack will be used to supply power to all components. All components will be securely mounted to ensure stability and proper functioning of the robot. 2.2 Sensor Integration Sensors will be integrated to detect fire and gas leakage in the environment. ●​ The MQ-2 gas sensor will continuously monitor air quality and detect gases such as LPG, methane, and smoke. ●​ Multiple flame sensors will be placed at different positions (left, center, right) to detect the direction of fire. ●​ An optional ultrasonic sensor will be used to detect obstacles and measure distance. Sensor data will be sent to the microcontroller for real-time processing. 2.3 Movement Control The robot’s movement system will be controlled using programmed logic. ●​ The L298N motor driver will receive signals from the microcontroller. ●​ Based on flame sensor input, the robot will move toward the fire source. ●​ The robot will be programmed to: ○​ Move forward ○​ Turn left or right depending on fire direction ○​ Stop when close to the fire This ensures accurate navigation toward the detected hazard.

Introduction Fire accidents and gas leakages are common hazards in homes, shops, and small businesses. These incidents can cause serious damage to property and may also threaten human life.​ ​ Most workplaces rely on basic safety systems such as fire extinguishers and smoke alarms, which require human presence. However, fires or gas leaks may occur when no one is present, leading to delayed response.​ ​ This project proposes a Firefighting and Gas Detection Robot that can automatically detect fire and gas leakage, provide alerts, and assist in extinguishing small fires. 2. Proposed Methodology The development of the Firefighting and Gas Detection Robot will be carried out through several structured steps, combining hardware implementation and software control. 2.1 Hardware Setup At the initial stage, all physical components of the robot will be assembled. ●​ A PVC board or robot chassis will be used as the base platform. ●​ Two DC motors with wheels will be mounted to enable movement. ●​ The ESP32 microcontroller will be installed as the main control unit. ●​ The motor driver (L298N) will be connected to control the motors. ●​ A battery pack will be used to supply power to all components. All components will be securely mounted to ensure stability and proper functioning of the robot. 2.2 Sensor Integration Sensors will be integrated to detect fire and gas leakage in the environment. ●​ The MQ-2 gas sensor will continuously monitor air quality and detect gases such as LPG, methane, and smoke. ●​ Multiple flame sensors will be placed at different positions (left, center, right) to detect the direction of fire. ●​ An optional ultrasonic sensor will be used to detect obstacles and measure distance. Sensor data will be sent to the microcontroller for real-time processing. 2.3 Movement Control The robot’s movement system will be controlled using programmed logic. ●​ The L298N motor driver will receive signals from the microcontroller. ●​ Based on flame sensor input, the robot will move toward the fire source. ●​ The robot will be programmed to: ○​ Move forward ○​ Turn left or right depending on fire direction ○​ Stop when close to the fire This ensures accurate navigation toward the detected hazard.
